source_text: Sic Core et Dathan et Abiron qui sibi contra Moysen et Aaron sacerdotem sacrificandi licentiam uindicare conati sunt poenas statim pro suis conatibus pependerunt. terra conpagibus ruptis in profundum sinus patuit, stantes adque uiuentes recedentis soli hiatus absorbuit, nec tantum eos qui auctores fuerant Dei indignantis ira percussit, sed et ceteros ducentos quinquaginta participes eiusdem furoris et comites qui coagulati cum isdem simul ad audaciam fuerant exiens a Domino ignis properata ultione consumpsit, admonens scilicet et ostendens contra Deum fieri quicquid inprobi fuerint ad destruendam ordinationem Dei humana uoluntate conati. sic et Ozias rex cum turibulum ferens et contra legem Dei sacrificium sibi uiolenter adsumens resistente sibi Azaria sacerdote obtemperare nollet et cedere, diuina indignatione confusus et leprae uarietate in fronte maculatus est, ea parte corporis notatus offenso Domino ubi signantur qui Dominum promerentur. et filii Aaron, qui inposuerunt altari ignem alienum quem non praeceperat Dominus, in conspectu statim Domini uindicantis extincti sunt.
thought_title: Old Testament examples of divine punishment for rebellion against God's ordering
orientation: Cyprian is continuing his warning against those who break away from the Church, now giving Old Testament examples of divine punishment for those who usurped priestly authority.
pass_a_gloss: Thus Korah and Dathan and Abiram, who attempted to claim for themselves against Moses and Aaron the priest the license of sacrificing, paid the penalties immediately for their attempts. The earth, its joints broken, opened into the depth of its bosom, the gaping of the receding ground swallowed them standing and alive, and not only did the anger of the indignant God strike those who had been the authors, but also the other two hundred fifty participants and companions of the same madness, who had been joined together with them at the same time for the audacity, fire going out from the Lord consumed them with swift vengeance, warning of course and showing that whatever wicked men have attempted by human will for destroying the ordering of God is done against God. Thus also king Uzziah, when carrying the censer and violently taking to himself sacrifice against the law of God, with Azariah the priest resisting him, was unwilling to obey and yield, confounded by divine indignation and marked with the variety of leprosy on his forehead, marked on that part of the body, the Lord having been offended, where those who merit the Lord are signed. And the sons of Aaron, who placed on the altar strange fire which the Lord had not commanded, were extinguished immediately in the sight of the avenging Lord.

choices.why: Keeps the legal force of licentia as an unauthorized claim to a right, matching Cyprian's point about usurping priestly authority.
Conatus implies effort or undertaking, often with a negative sense of presumption; 'attempts' preserves the idea of an unlawful endeavor.
Compages means a joining or fastening; rendering it as 'joints' keeps the vivid physical image of the earth's structure breaking apart.
rejected: the earth with its bonds broken

choices.english: opened into the depth of its bosom
choices.why: Sinus literally means bosom or hollow; keeping it preserves the personified image of the earth opening its depths.
Varietas suggests the mottled or varied appearance of the skin disease; keeping 'variety' is literal and vivid.

choices.english: where those who merit the Lord are signed
choices.why: Signare refers to the sign of the cross or marking; 'signed' preserves the liturgical sense of being marked by God, contrasting with Uzziah's mark of punishment.
rejected: where those who please the Lord are marked
where those who win the Lord's favor are sealed

bible_refs.note: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram rebel against Moses and Aaron; the earth opens and fire consumes the 250 men.
King Uzziah takes up the censer against the priests and is struck with leprosy on his forehead.
Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, offer strange fire and are consumed by fire from the Lord.

pass_b_english: So Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, who tried to claim for themselves the license of sacrificing against Moses and Aaron the priest, paid the penalty for their attempts at once. The earth, its joints broken, opened into the depth of its bosom; the gaping of the ground as it gave way swallowed them standing and alive. Nor did the anger of an indignant God strike only those who had been the instigators, but the other two hundred and fifty who shared in the same madness and were their companions, joined together with them in the same audacity, were consumed by fire that went out from the Lord in swift vengeance. This warns and shows that whatever wicked people have attempted by human will to destroy God's ordering is done against God. So also King Uzziah, when he carried a censer and violently took the sacrifice to himself against the law of God, refused to obey and yield to Azariah the priest who resisted him. He was confounded by divine indignation and marked on his forehead with the variety of leprosy, marked on that part of the body where those who merit the Lord are signed, because he had offended the Lord. And the sons of Aaron, who placed on the altar strange fire that the Lord had not commanded, were extinguished at once in the sight of the avenging Lord.

last_rejected.quote: because he had offended the Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: ea parte corporis notatus offenso Domino ubi signantur qui Dominum promerentur
last_rejected.why: Misreads syntax: 'offenso Domino' is ablative absolute ('the Lord having been offended'), not a causal clause about Uzziah offending the Lord.
last_rejected.fix: marked on that part of the body where those who merit the Lord are signed, the Lord having been offended.
last_rejected.ruling: Ablative absolute 'offenso Domino' still yields 'because he had offended the Lord'; meaning unchanged.

last_rejected.why: 'Uarietate' here means 'disfigurement' or 'discoloration' from leprosy, not 'variety' in the modern sense of diverse types.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Varietas' can mean 'variety' of leprosy; within normal range, not a major mistranslation.
